speaker: Doctor
text: I need to understand the timing and nature of your symptoms first. How many days have you had the diarrhea, and does it contain blood or mucus? Also, have you experienced any fever or severe abdominal pain?

speaker: Patient
text: 58-year-old female. The patient has been treated for community-acquired pneumonia with levofloxacin on the medical floor. She reports developing watery diarrhea with at least 9 episodes within the last two days, accompanied by lower abdominal discomfort and cramping.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for those details; the timing and recent use of levofloxacin strongly suggest antibiotic-associated diarrhea, likely caused by *Clostridioides difficile*. REQUEST TEST: C. diff toxin assay. Have you noticed any blood in the stool, or have you developed a high fever recently?

text: RESULTS: C. diff toxin assay: Not specified

text: My main symptom is Watery diarrhea. I also have Lower abdominal discomfort, Abdominal cramping.

text: Past medical history: Currently being treated for community-acquired pneumonia. No other significant past medical history. Social history: Non-smoker, does not consume alcohol. No recent travel or dietary changes reported.

speaker: Patient
text: No fever, no recent antibiotics usage apart from levofloxacin for pneumonia, no vomiting, no blood in stool. To keep my notes clear, please give only one final answer and keep it to a single direct conclusion.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: C. difficile infection (CDI) secondary to levofloxacin therapy.
